race_name: Gran Fondo Samoëns – Montagnes du Giffre

top_categories.workout_context: 177 miles. Your legs will beg to quit after 120. This trains the power output you need from mile 130 onward.
26,574ft of climbing means repeated surges above threshold. VO2max work is how you survive the fifth climb, not just the first.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Gran Fondo Samoëns – Montagnes du Giffre's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.
At Gran Fondo Samoëns – Montagnes du Giffre, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
26,574ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
150ft/mi means long efforts at or near FTP on every climb. If your threshold cracks at minute 15, you'll walk the rest.
Gran Fondo Samoëns – Montagnes du Giffre's mixed terrain forces constant power changes. Accelerate over rises and out of corners, settle on the open road, and repeat for 177 miles.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 177 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Gran Fondo Samoëns – Montagnes du Giffre. Train it until it feels boring.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 26,574ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
177 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.
Low-cadence force work for 26,574ft of climbing. The slow, grinding ascents where you can't spin—you push.

race_overlay.nutrition: Fueling for 177 miles requires a practiced plan matched to expected duration, intensity, tolerance, and the course's confirmed feed or commercial resupply options. Rehearse the plan on long rides, begin early, carry redundant fuel, and avoid treating a fixed total-calorie estimate as a race prescription.
race_overlay.altitude: Gran Fondo Samoëns – Montagnes du Giffre with 26,574ft of climbing, much of it above 8,000ft demands altitude preparation. Arrive 5–7 days early for acclimatization. Expect 5–15% power reduction at altitude. Increase iron intake 4 weeks out. Hydrate aggressively — altitude increases fluid loss by 20–40%.
race_overlay.terrain: Mixed terrain at Gran Fondo Samoëns – Montagnes du Giffre requires surface adaptability. Include weekly rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, VO2max, and Race Simulation to prepare you for 177 miles of mixed terrain in Samoëns, Haute-Savoie, France.
